intro: Covers the US session of Friday 30 October (a sharp tech-led sell-off). This is the delayed 08:15 edition: the SPI 200 futures figure is a range because sources differ on level, and one bond-yield figure was reconciled between two sources (see footnotes). No sector breakdown was available.
footnotes: US 10-year: Yahoo shows 4.929% (-6 bp, prior 4.989%); Trading Economics shows 4.934% with a negligible change. The -6 bp figure is used because it matches the prior close we recorded on 30 October.
VIX: Yahoo and FNArena show a prior close of 17.20; Trading Economics shows an unchanged print. Yahoo used.
Brent: Trading Economics 113.43 (+2.37%); FNArena 113.95; Yahoo's live blog cited about US$112 intraday. Front-month contract differences.
Spot gold: a futures quote (GC=F) was US$3,898.90, -3.29%.
Index closes are Yahoo/Trading Economics official quotes; intraday news text cited slightly larger Dow and S&P falls.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (Dec 2026) are slightly lower but sources differ on size: TradingView and FNArena show 8,914 (-0.04%) as at about 08:11 AEDT, while Investing.com shows 8,901.5 (-0.34%) for the Friday close. Taking the midpoint (about 8,908, -0.19%, approximate) implies an ASX 200 open roughly 17 points, or 0.19%, lower, near 8,891. The range is -0.04% to -0.34%; the small move looks mild against the size of the Wall Street fall, so treat the figure with caution. The ASX 200 closed Friday at 8,908.10, up 0.18%.

local_events: RBA decision due tomorrow (Tuesday 3 November), with markets pricing a 25 bp hike.
No other scheduled Australian data was verified for today.
what_moved: Disappointing mega-cap tech earnings drove a broad sell-off on the last trading day of October, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2.86% and the S&P 500 1.82%. Alphabet fell roughly 12% on a quarterly miss and Intel slumped on weak guidance, feeding concern over the return on AI spending. Spot gold fell 3.62% to a one-year low while oil rose on reports the US could resume strikes on Iran, and Treasury yields eased as bonds rallied. S&P 500 sector performance was not available.

news.headline: Tech earnings misses trigger the worst Nasdaq day since June
news.summary: Alphabet and Amazon reported rare misses and Intel gave weak guidance, hitting chip and AI-linked names as October closed. The Nasdaq lost about 5% for the month.

news.headline: Gold hits a one-year low
news.summary: Spot gold fell 3.62% to US$3,875.84/oz, its weakest in a year, as the sell-off hit broader risk assets.

news.headline: Markets price a possible December Fed hike
news.summary: Third-quarter US GDP grew 3.4% and September PCE rose 0.5% m/m, with core at 3.1% y/y; Fed officials Musalem and Barkin said rates may need to rise. CME FedWatch implied roughly a 72-75% chance of a December hike.

news.headline: Treasury yields at seven-week lows
news.summary: The 10-year yield ended near 4.93% as bonds rallied on the equity sell-off, having fallen about 36 bp over October.

news.headline: Oil rises on Iran strike reports
news.summary: Brent finished about 2.4% higher at US$113.43/bbl on reports the US could resume strikes on Iran.

news.headline: Binance hack knocks bitcoin
news.summary: A reported US$6.3bn exploit at the exchange pushed bitcoin down about 5%, to around US$76,600.

news.headline: RBA expected to hike on Tuesday
news.summary: Markets price a 25 bp increase to 4.85% at the 3 November meeting, at about 88% probability.

coming_up: Tuesday 3 November: RBA rate decision (AEDT), and US midterm elections (US time), with results arriving Wednesday morning in Sydney. NAB reports Thursday 5 November and Macquarie on Friday 6 November.
